query: how to make an ai agent ask before it acts
title: How to make an AI agent ask before it acts | 50agents
description: Make an AI agent ask before it acts: sort actions by risk, hold risky ones in an approval the software enforces, show the full action, plan for silence.
h1: How to make an AI agent ask before it acts
answer: Sort its actions into "does alone" and "asks first", and use a tool that holds sends, payments, deletions and access changes until you approve.
Each approval should show exactly what will happen and wait for an answer.

root.q: Does the action change anything, or only read?

then.why: Reading email, searching a CRM or a web page breaks nothing. It shows up in the log.

then.q: Does it move money, delete, or change access?

then.answer: Always ask, whatever else you loosen
then.why: Payments, refunds, deletions, shared files and new people are hard to undo. They wait for a yes, every time.

then.q: Does it reach anyone outside your business?

then.answer: Ask first, with the full text shown
then.why: A sent email cannot be unsent. Approve it until you approve that kind unchanged for weeks.

then.answer: Ask first at the start, then loosen
then.why: Changing a record in your own apps can be undone. Once you approve it unchanged for weeks, let it run alone.

sections.h2: Why "ask me first" in the prompt is not enough

body.p: Tell a model to check with you before anything risky and it usually will. But prompt text guides the model and enforces nothing. For anything that moves money, a person should approve each call in the software.
The test: if the AI agent skipped the question, would the action still go through? If yes, you have a polite request, not an approval.

ul: **Who is asking:** which AI agent, on which run.
**Exactly what will happen:** the recipient and full text, the record and new value, or the amount and who gets it.
**Why:** one line of its reasoning, so you can spot a wrong premise.
**A way to change it,** not only yes or no.
**It stays open:** an unanswered approval waits; it never expires into "yes".

steps.title: List every action it can take
steps.body: From its apps: read, create, update, send, delete, share. You will be surprised how many it has.

steps.title: Put each one in a group
steps.body: Does alone, asks first, or always asks. Use the chooser above. When in doubt, put it in asks first; you can move it later.

steps.title: Remove what it never needs
steps.body: An action it never uses should not be there at all. Fewer actions means fewer approvals and less to go wrong.

steps.title: Pick one place for approvals
steps.body: One place you check a few times a day, on your phone too. Approvals scattered across email, chat and dashboards get missed.

note.text: Fifty approvals a day and you stop reading them. Trim what asks, and group low-risk items into one daily report.

steps.title: Watch the approve-without-edits rate
steps.body: If you approve one kind of action unchanged for a few weeks, consider letting it run alone. If you edit most, fix the instructions.

steps.title: Plan for retries
steps.body: An approved action can run twice if the tool crashes in between. Ask your tool how it makes approved actions safe to repeat.

captain.line: 50agents puts every approval in one place, Needs you. Anything that spends money, reaches people outside your workspace or changes access asks first, and stays open until you answer.

wrong.title: Approving without context
wrong.body: The card says "Send email?" without the text. Never approve what you cannot see in full.

wrong.title: Nobody answers
wrong.body: The approval sits for a week and the moment passes. Check at fixed times, and give the AI agent a rule for stale items.

wrong.title: The AI agent decides when to ask
wrong.body: If asking is up to the AI, one day it will not ask. Put the rule in the tool's settings, not only in the prompt.

wrong.title: Approved twice
wrong.body: A retry after a crash sends the same email again. Prefer tools that record each approved action once.

faqs.q: What is human in the loop for AI agents?
faqs.a: A person approves certain actions before they happen. It differs from reviewing a report after the fact, which some call human on the loop.

faqs.q: Can I approve from my phone?
faqs.a: Pick a tool where you can. Approvals that wait for a desk slow the AI agent down to your desk hours.

faqs.q: When can I let it act without asking?
faqs.a: When you have approved that kind of action unchanged many times, and a mistake would be cheap and easy to undo. Never for payments, deletions or access.
